why: How a number becomes text, as value and text pairs, so that a second engine in any language can check its own writer against the rule of language.md section 5.5 without parsing this repository's source. Every row is one binary64 value spelled two ways, as its bit pattern and as a decimal a JSON reader turns into the same value, and the text the rule writes for it. Both directions hold: writing the value gives the text, and reading the text gives the value, with negative zero reading back as zero. The rows are the boundary cases: the two thresholds where the layout changes, the extremes of the double range, the zeros, and values whose shortest digits are not their exact expansion. tests/emit/number-text.test.ts holds this engine to every row and refuses a file that drops a boundary.
